markdown_report:
**Selected direction: calibrate NextItNet diagnostics against independently verified inference faults before expanding them.** At 20% progress, probe reliability is a feasible next step; recommendation improvement requires separate validation evidence.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Sampled-training pairwise accuracy spans 96.64–99.33%, establishing sampled separation without held-out HR@10 evidence. (2) Local-signal measurements lack a verified scorer/loss/sampler contract; definitions cannot replace implementation support. (3) Unknown category provenance prevents defensible category aggregation. These gaps favor contract verification before additional diagnostic complexity.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Mutation testing [1,5,6] motivates seeded faults, but representative faults and independent injection verification remain essential. (2) Sanity-check and numerical-accuracy work [2,7] motivates separate threshold calibration, exact structural assertions, and scale-aware numerical comparisons. (3) NextItNet’s causal contract [3] supplies testable relations; framework documentation [8,9] reveals hook and state-restoration pitfalls.

These insights organize three directions: provenance, diagnostic reliability, and prospective recommendation improvement.

| Direction | Existing evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Provenance | Training-prefix candidate audits | Verified category and contract |
| Reliability | Passing identity/batch checks | Independent fault witnesses and transfer |
| Improvement | Qualitative recency concerns | Fixed-protocol validation evidence |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation effort.

- **Fault-calibrated probes [1–3,5–9]: 4/6/6.** Originality: useful family-specific integration; established testing methods. Potential: exposes blind spots; designed mutants can encourage shortcuts. Difficulty: bounded inference; isolation and independent witnesses require substantial integration.
- **Explicit diagnostic contract: 3/6/2.** Originality: resolves observed provenance gaps; standard engineering. Potential: enables faithful audits; no direct ranking improvement. Difficulty: small schema change; requires verified host facts.
- **Block-by-lag activation patching [4]: 5/6/6.** Originality: family-specific adaptation; established intervention method. Potential: localizes computational influence; corruption-dependent conclusions. Difficulty: avoids retraining; hook boundaries remain demanding.

**Chosen algorithm.** First establish provenance and a reproducible execution contract. Freeze probes, fault operators, control suites, numerical thresholds, and denominators before assessment. Use disjoint calibration/assessment users and reserve additional operator families for transfer assessment. Independently witness faults through executed indices or forbidden tensor dependencies; the diagnostic never receives mutation identity. Position-coded features expose incorrect readout, while intermediate-position suffix interventions expose future leakage.

```text
for category in four_routes:
    verify contract; partition identified training users
    calibrate tolerances on trusted clean controls; freeze
    for declared control or fault:
        independently record execution witness
        run frozen probes without mutation identity
    report coverage, detections, control alarms and runtime
```

Distinguish installed, witnessed, unresolved, and detected faults. Report category-specific user-level endpoints; repeated mutations remain clustered. With 32 independent sampled users and zero alarms, the one-sided 95% binomial upper bound is 8.94% [10], conditional on the declared endpoint and sampling assumptions.

Preserve diagnostic interfaces, actual `view.model`, complete execution state, and final-nonpadding production readout. Use isolated diagnostic inputs and exception-safe hooks; verify successful and failed probes preserve subsequent execution. Temporary faults never enter checkpoints or prediction. Retain fixed seeds, splits, limits, evaluator, and exactly one checkpoint per category. Synthetic-fault success alone supports neither general defect detection nor HR@10 improvement.

idea.description: Add a bounded fault-calibration panel to the existing NextItNet diagnostic adapter, measuring whether frozen probes detect independently witnessed inference faults while accepting verified semantics-preserving controls. Establish diagnostic provenance and execution contracts first, and assess transfer beyond design-time fault operators separately.
idea.motivation: Existing diagnostics demonstrate sampled training separation and passing identity controls, but do not establish detection sensitivity. Missing scorer contracts and unknown category provenance restrict interpretation. At early research progress, checking diagnostic reliability is practical, provided that fault verification is independent of probe alarms, thresholds are frozen before assessment, and synthetic-fault results are not presented as evidence of recommendation improvement or general fault coverage.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), sample_batch and every ModelView interface. view.model remains the actual trained NextItNet nn.Module; preserve view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Extend metrics and metric_definitions rather than replacing existing measurements.

Require explicit category identity from the host's existing routing metadata. Do not infer category from catalog size, user counts or filenames. If unavailable, report category-dependent aggregation as null with a reason. Establish the diagnostic contract as the first implementation step, rather than expanding an audit whose provenance is unresolved. A descriptive objective definition does not verify the scorer, loss, sampler, exclusions, masks or reduction; unsupported objective-dependent metrics remain null.

Use only permitted public training histories and available titles, descriptions and timestamps. Ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores and simulator diversity/conformity traits remain unavailable despite generic dataset examples. Observed interactions do not establish ownership, compatibility or current intent.

Select at most 64 identified users per category after deterministic ID sorting, using a local seed-42 generator. Allocate 32 calibration and 32 assessment users without overlap, or document smaller available counts and the exact allocation. Record selected IDs, selection rules and partition assignments in trial-local artifacts. This is a diagnostic partition of training users, not a change to the supplied training/validation splits. Use actual mapped item IDs, baseline truncation, left padding and the largest nonzero sequence index; skip all-padding sequences. Anonymous loader rows remain position-level observations, not independent users. Training-prefix targets remain in-sample and may have influenced fitting.

Predeclare exact probe implementations, clean controls, fault operators, operator parameters, candidate IDs, input lengths, comparison positions, precision, hardware settings, tolerance rules and denominators. Retain the existing diagnostic candidate panels where their contracts match; document any separate panel. No validation labels or hidden test files are needed for this audit.

Calibrate numerical tolerances on separate, trusted clean calibration users using identical-input reruns and supported semantics-preserving transformations. Use the declared comparison |a-b| <= atol + rtol*|b|, where b is the reference output. The previous atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5 are starting values, not universal guarantees. Choose and document the output-scale rule before assessment; for example, freeze rtol and set atol to the maximum positive residual max(|a-b|-rtol*|b|,0) across the complete prespecified clean calibration suite, with a declared numerical floor. Report the resulting tolerances and raw discrepancies. This empirical maximum does not guarantee future specificity, especially with only 32 calibration users. Never enlarge thresholds after observing assessment faults. If clean discrepancies are unexpectedly large or structurally unexplained, mark calibration invalid rather than automatically absorbing them.

Calibrate and assess the maximum discrepancy across each user's prespecified suite so that the user-level alarm endpoint reflects the suite's multiple comparisons. Structural assertions remain exact and separate: dataset routing, candidate identity, padding/readout indices and checkpoint compatibility cannot be repaired by enlarging numerical tolerances. Semantics-preserving controls include batch permutation and adding or removing leading padding only when supported by the inspected implementation and width contract. PyTorch does not guarantee bitwise equality between mathematically equivalent batched and individual computations.

Use temporary execution functions and scoped hooks on the same network; never instantiate or fit another predictor. Verify hooks execute through the actual production-compatible entry point: log2feats may bypass root forward hooks, and direct calls to module.forward bypass module hooks. Before assessment, attach a counter and a sentinel exception to a child module the entry point must execute; assert that the counter advances and the exception reaches the caller. Remove the sentinel before measurement. Register handles inside try/finally and always remove them; always_call=True does not provide automatic cleanup.

For the count-minus-one readout fault, first test the readout helper with position-coded synthetic B x L x D features and varied nonempty left-padded history lengths, including short and full-width histories. Independently record the executed index, its selected position code, and the expected largest nonzero index. Full-width histories can conceal this fault. Distinguish a unit-level readout-contract test from an end-to-end model-output test: a faulty index can be witnessed even when learned features happen to yield indistinguishable scores. Do not count synthetic feature results as recommendation evidence. Skip count-minus-one behavior on empty inputs rather than allowing index -1.

For future leakage, independently establish an active forbidden dependency at an intermediate valid position. A temporary execution variant may replace its feature with a later valid feature; label this injected future-feature dependence, not a reproduced convolution bug. Verify the installed path by tracing indices and tensor provenance, and record an independent perturbation or dependency witness on inputs separate from the probe's assessment pair. Then run the frozen causal probe: change only a later valid suffix while holding the prefix, lengths, padding, scored items and readout position fixed, and compare earlier features or scores. Final-position inference alone cannot expose access to future positions. A differentiable dependency check may be used in a separately isolated local test if needed, but the default audit remains evaluation-only without gradients and never changes parameter gradients.

Only include padding-mask suppression when the actual implementation exposes a safe, verifiable hook. Verify the altered mask path independently and distinguish installed suppression from observed nonzero padding propagation. Unsupported faults are null, not assumed detected. Retain unmanifested mutants as unresolved; finite-input survival does not prove semantic equivalence.

Keep injection verification separate from probe scoring. The verification process records structural witnesses, installation status and any independently observed behavioral effect. The probe receives only its ordinary inputs and outputs, without mutation labels, names, flags or witness metadata. Successful injection must never be defined by the probe's own alarm. Distinguish installed faults, structurally witnessed deviations, independently witnessed numerical effects, probe detections and clean-control alarms. Use endpoint-specific denominators: an exact readout oracle evaluates witnessed index faults, whereas a numerical causality detector evaluates independently active forbidden dependencies. Report all eligible cases, installation failures, unsupported cases and unresolved cases alongside conditional detection rates to prevent denominator inflation.

Reduce shortcut learning by freezing probes and thresholds before assessment and reserving operator families or alternative implementations that were not used to design them. Disjoint users alone assess input transfer, not transfer to unseen defect mechanisms. Report design-time and reserved-operator results separately. Documented real bugs can strengthen transfer evidence when already available within the authorized implementation context; do not fetch other trials, checkpoints, datasets or pretrained weights. If no reserved operators or real bugs are available, mark general fault-transfer evidence unavailable. No diagnostic classifier or auxiliary predictor is trained.

For each category and declared fault family, define one binary endpoint per user, such as any clean-control alarm across its fixed suite or detection of at least one independently witnessed fault instance. State whether an any-instance endpoint can hide poor instance-level coverage; also report raw instance counts without treating them as independent users. Report category-specific counts and rates before any equal-weight four-category macro average. Macro summaries require all four categories and compatible endpoint definitions. User bootstrap intervals resample complete user vectors within category, preserving mutation clustering and paired comparisons. They condition on fitted models, declared inputs and operators and exclude training-seed and adaptive-search uncertainty.

At zero alarms or perfect detection, ordinary bootstrap intervals collapse. For a prespecified binary endpoint under independent Bernoulli user-sampling assumptions, report exact binomial bounds and their assumptions. With 32 users, zero alarms gives a one-sided 95% upper bound of 1-0.05^(1/32)=8.94%; 32 detections gives a one-sided lower bound of 91.06%. Two-sided 95% intervals are approximately [0,10.89%] and [89.11%,100%]. These do not apply to mutation instances, establish universal detection, or automatically describe finite-population sampling without replacement. For the latter sampling target, use a finite-population procedure when justified or label binomial bounds as a superpopulation reference. Do not derive a macro interval by treating the four categories as independent mutation observations or by averaging marginal interval endpoints.

Perform ordinary probes in evaluation mode without gradients. Save every module's individual training flag and restore flags individually in finally; recursive train(flag) can overwrite mixed module states. Preserve Python and NumPy RNG state, Torch CPU and relevant CUDA RNG state, and the state of explicit generators used by the audit. torch.random.fork_rng can protect Torch CPU and selected CUDA states but does not cover Python, NumPy or arbitrary generators.

For verified exception-safe isolation, snapshot cloned parameters, every buffer including nonpersistent buffers, existing parameter gradients including None status, and the hook handles installed by this audit. A plain state_dict snapshot aliases live tensor storage and excludes nonpersistent buffers. Avoid parameter or buffer mutation in the first place; restore tensor contents under no_grad where necessary without replacing Parameter objects. Use bounded snapshots, placing backups on CPU if needed, and account for transfer/runtime overhead. Preserve any additional inspected model-local cache or mutable execution state; if complete isolation cannot be established, declare that limitation and do not claim unchanged training execution.

DataLoader iteration can advance samplers, workers and prefetch queues even when global RNG state is restored. Use already cached diagnostic batches supplied outside the continuing training iterator, or an isolated diagnostic loader with independent generators and sampler state. Prefer constructing identified-user panels directly from permitted histories. Do not consume the active training loader to populate a new audit cache and then claim the next training batch is unchanged. Existing diagnostic loader consumption must also be documented and isolated for a full preservation claim.

Before accepting the implementation, run a bounded preservation regression for both successful probes and an injected exception. Compare untouched and audited continuations sequentially from identical saved starting states using the same model object; no additional independently trained model is required. Assert audit hooks are removed, preexisting hooks remain, flags/tensors/gradients/RNGs match, fixed prediction scores match within the frozen numerical contract, and the next training batch agrees. Where optimizer and loader state are available, replay one identical next optimization step from the same restored state and compare parameters and optimizer state, then restore the original state. This is a bounded regression that consumes the shared budget, not a second trained predictor. If the adapter cannot access optimizer or iterator state, expose those checks as unavailable and avoid a full training-continuation guarantee.

Fault wrappers and snapshots never enter training checkpoints, the predictor writer or working/predict.py. Verify original scores before and after the panel on fixed examples, including failure paths. Bound and record synchronized GPU runtime, forward/scoring counts, precision, snapshot overhead and skip reasons; synchronize before and after measurement to exclude previously queued work. Diagnostics consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. Run only the declared bounded panel rather than expanding fault searches adaptively.

The interpreter prompt serializes measured metrics, definitions, counts, witnesses, exclusions and missing evidence. It distinguishes original-execution control failures from injected-fault detections, design-time operators from reserved operators, and exact structural checks from numerical tests. It prohibits claims about general defect detection, held-out gains, latent intent, ownership or compatibility without corresponding evidence. Activation patching and recency-focused training remain separate future hypotheses; qualitative feedback alone does not establish their mechanism.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, supplied splits and evaluator. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, with exactly one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category. No auxiliary fitted scorer, checkpoint averaging, score fusion or additional production model is introduced. Production readout remains the final nonpadding position. Any later architectural inference change must update the embedded predictor writer consistently. Subsequent training interventions are selected solely by the unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10; record configurations tried and never use hidden tests.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        # Existing diagnostics must also use cached or isolated diagnostic inputs.
        states = snapshot_cloned_tensors_buffers_gradients_modes_and_rngs()
        handles = []
        result = initialize_existing_metric_schema()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            category = explicit_host_category_or_unavailable()
            contract = verify_mapping_scorer_entrypoint_and_input_contract()
            diagnostic_inputs = cached_inputs_or_isolated_loader(train_loader)
            result = run_existing_bounded_diagnostics(diagnostic_inputs)
            users = select_sorted_identified_training_users(cap=64, local_seed=42)
            calibration, assessment = recorded_disjoint_partition(users, 32, 32)
            examples = build_baseline_left_padded_examples(calibration, assessment)
            verify_child_hook_counter_and_sentinel_through_actual_entrypoint()
            with no_grad():
                original_scores = score_fixed_original_examples(examples)
                run_exact_readout_oracle_with_position_coded_features()
                tolerances = calibrate_clean_user_suite_maxima(calibration)
                freeze_probes_thresholds_operators_endpoints_and_denominators()
                for variant in declared_controls_and_fault_operators:
                    if not verify_variant_supported_by_actual_model(variant):
                        record_unsupported_with_reason(variant)
                        continue
                    with scoped_execution_variant(self.view.model, variant, handles):
                        witness = independently_verify_indices_or_dependencies(
                            separate_verification_inputs(assessment))
                        # Scoring code cannot access variant identity or witness.
                        measurements = run_frozen_probes(
                            ordinary_assessment_inputs(assessment), tolerances)
                    record_installed_witnessed_unresolved_detected_and_alarm_counts(
                        variant, witness, measurements)
                verify_original_scores_restored(original_scores, tolerances)
        finally:
            remove_only_audit_hooks(handles)
            restore_cloned_tensors_buffers_gradients_individual_modes_and_rngs(states)
            record_synchronized_runtime_forward_counts_and_overhead()
        summarize_category_user_endpoints_and_instance_counts_separately(result)
        add_clustered_intervals_and_endpoint_appropriate_boundary_bounds(result)
        record_reserved_operator_transfer_evidence_or_unavailable(result)
        append_exact_populations_definitions_missingness_and_limitations(result)
        return result

# Integration regression, using the same model sequentially from saved state:
for outcome in [successful_probe, injected_exception]:
    compare_untouched_and_audited_continuations_from_identical_state(outcome)
    assert_hooks_modes_tensors_gradients_rngs_and_scores_restored()
    verify_next_batch_and_next_optimizer_step_if_interfaces_available()
    restore_original_state()

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return serialize_metrics_and_definitions_with_instructions(
        raw_diagnosis,
        distinguish_original_controls_from_injected_faults=True,
        distinguish_structural_from_numerical_evidence=True,
        require_independent_witnesses_and_explicit_denominators=True,
        separate_design_time_and_reserved_operator_results=True,
        prohibit_unmeasured_validation_general_transfer_or_preference_claims=True)

originality.positive: Combines independent execution witnesses, exact readout oracles, separate numerical calibration and operator-transfer assessment within the existing NextItNet adapter.
originality.negative: Mutation testing, metamorphic relations and isolation regressions are established techniques; the contribution is a careful family-specific integration rather than a new learning algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Can expose concrete diagnostic blind spots and implementation defects before scarce training budget is spent on diagnostic-driven interventions.
future_potential.negative: Designed inference faults may poorly represent natural training defects, and no supplied evidence establishes transfer or improved validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses bounded inference on the existing trained network and requires no production architecture change or additional fitted predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Independent dependency witnesses, verified hook execution, complete exception-safe state restoration, loader isolation and continuation replay require substantial implementation access and careful integration.

related_work.title: [1] Mutation-Guided Metamorphic Testing
contributions: The supplied search summary describes selecting tests by their ability to detect mutated planners.
Motivates assessing diagnostic detection against explicitly seeded faults.
limitations: Planner evidence does not establish reliability for NextItNet or recommendation diagnostics.
Detection of designed mutants need not predict detection of naturally occurring defects.

related_work.title: [2] A Fresh Look at Sanity Checks for Saliency Methods
contributions: The supplied search summary identifies noise and similarity-measure problems in parameter-randomization sanity checks.
Motivates explicit numerical controls and separate calibration and assessment.
limitations: Saliency sanity checks do not directly validate sequential recommendation probes.
Its findings provide methodological guidance rather than evidence of NextItNet ranking gains.

related_work.title: [3] A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Introduces the NextItNet family of causal dilated convolutional residual models.
Provides architectural motivation for testing causal dependence, temporal reach and intermediate-position future invariance.
limitations: The family description cannot establish the exact behavior of the supplied implementation.
Theoretical receptive-field coverage does not establish useful influence or held-out ranking quality.

related_work.title: [4] Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: The supplied search summary highlights sensitivity to corruption choice, output metrics and patched layer windows.
Supports activation patching as a possible later computational-influence audit.
limitations: The evidence concerns language models rather than NextItNet.
Patching effects depend on intervention design and do not establish user intent or training-data causality.

related_work.title: [5] Just How Good Is Your Test Suite? An Empirical Study of Mutant and Real Fault Detection
contributions: Studies the relationship between mutant detection and real-fault detection.
Motivates testing transfer beyond design-time mutants rather than treating mutation scores as universal fault coverage.
limitations: Observed relationships in studied software do not establish transfer to NextItNet.
Independent fault witnesses and realistic operator selection remain necessary.

related_work.title: [6] What Are We Really Testing in Mutation Testing for Machine Learning? A Critical Reflection
contributions: Questions whether machine-learning mutations consistently represent implementation bugs.
Supports separating artificial behavioral changes from realistic defect-detection claims.
limitations: Does not supply a validated NextItNet fault taxonomy.
Does not establish which proposed inference mutations predict real recommendation failures.

related_work.title: [7] PyTorch Numerical Accuracy
contributions: Documents numerical differences between mathematically equivalent computations, including batched and individual execution.
Supports declared absolute-plus-relative tolerances rather than universal bitwise equality.
limitations: Does not prescribe suitable tolerances for this model or score scale.
Numerical thresholds cannot replace exact structural assertions or guarantee clean-control specificity.

related_work.title: [8] PyTorch Module Documentation
contributions: Documents forward-hook invocation, handle removal, module modes, parameters and buffers.
Supports verifying hook execution through the actual entry point and preserving individual module state.
limitations: Root hooks do not automatically cover custom methods such as log2feats.
Framework APIs alone do not establish isolation of model-local caches, loaders or optimizer continuation.

related_work.title: [9] PyTorch Data Loading Documentation
contributions: Documents data-loading randomness and generator-dependent execution.
Motivates isolated diagnostic loaders or cached inputs instead of consuming an active training iterator.
limitations: Restoring global RNG state does not rewind sampler, worker or prefetch execution.
Exact continuation checks require access to the actual loader and training workflow.

related_work.title: [10] SciPy Binomial Proportion Confidence Intervals
contributions: Provides exact binomial confidence intervals, including boundary outcomes where ordinary bootstrap intervals collapse.
Supports explicit uncertainty for prespecified binary user-level endpoints under stated sampling assumptions.
limitations: Repeated mutations within a user are not independent binomial observations.
Binomial bounds require an appropriate sampling model and do not automatically cover finite-population sampling or macro-average uncertainty.

related_work.title: DeepMutation: A Neural Mutation Tool
contributions: Provides an example of mutation-based testing for neural systems.
Motivates explicit operator specifications and separate evaluation of unseen operator families.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed NextItNet inference operators represent naturally occurring bugs.
Mutation success cannot substitute for independent fault verification or held-out recommendation evaluation.
